documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up (visit 2026-03-06)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 03/06/2026

Ms. Sears, 35, with Graves disease since early 2025, returns. Over recent months she has felt steadily more worn out, and her muscles feel weak. She is close to 8 kg under her usual weight although she eats large meals and snacks constantly because she is always hungry. She feels overheated even in air-conditioned rooms and sweats all day. At night she feels wired and can't settle; anxiety and restlessness are up. No recent illness, no travel.

Medications: she is not taking anything at present, including the methimazole started in August.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with Hashimoto hypothyroidism, maternal aunt with Graves disease, father with hypertension.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, elementary school teacher.

Exam: afebrile. Pulse 112, regular. BP 128/76. Weight 54.5 kg, BMI 20. Skin warm and moist. Fine tremor of both hands. Reflexes brisk and symmetric throughout. Heart and lungs normal. No proptosis, lid lag or conjunctival change. No leg edema. Thyroid diffusely enlarged, non-tender, without nodules.

Labs: TSH <0.01, free T4 3.8 ng/dL, total T3 240 ng/dL. CBC with differential and liver panel today are normal.

Assessment: Graves disease, uncontrolled, off therapy.

Plan:
1. Restart methimazole at 20 mg daily (two 10 mg tablets).
2. Propranolol 20 mg twice daily for heart rate and tremor.
3. Repeat TSH, free T4 and T3 in about 6 weeks, visit after.
4. We again discussed radioactive iodine and surgery as definitive options; she wants to retry medication first.
5. Reviewed reasons to stop methimazole and call: rash, fever, sore throat, jaundice.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up (visit 2026-05-11)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 05/11/2026

Graves disease, two months back on methimazole 20 mg daily with propranolol. She has taken both every day. Palpitations and sweating are much better and she is sleeping through most nights. Appetite settling. No rash, fever, sore throat or itching.

Labs 04/20/2026: TSH <0.01, free T4 2.2 ng/dL, total T3 192 ng/dL.

Exam: HR 82, BP 118/72, weight 56.6 kg. No tremor. Skin normal. Thyroid still enlarged, smooth, non-tender. No eye findings.

Assessment: Graves disease, improving on methimazole.

Plan:
1. Decrease methimazole to 10 mg daily.
2. Stop propranolol.
3. TSH, free T4, total T3 and CBC in 8 weeks; may be drawn at her primary care office with results sent here.
4. Follow-up visit after those results.

Endocrinology
